subject: Materials Science
title: Medical-Grade Polymers
description: A fast breakdown of Medical-Grade Polymers for builders.

hook.text: Silicone in breast implants, PTFE in vascular grafts, polyethylene in knee joints — polymers are everywhere in medicine.

buildup.text: Medical-grade polymers must be pure — no residual monomers, catalysts, or additives that could leach into tissue.

discovery.text: UHMWPE (ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene) lines hip and knee joints — its long chains resist wear for decades.

twist.text: Polymer wear particles trigger osteolysis — the immune system attacks debris, dissolving the bone around the implant.

climax.text: Crosslinked UHMWPE reduced wear particles by 90% — extending joint replacement life from 15 to over 25 years.

punchline.text: A plastic bearing in your joint, lasting decades — if the chemistry is right.

quiz.question: What problem did polymer wear particles cause in joint implants?
options: The joint became too stiff to move
Immune reaction to particles dissolved surrounding bone (osteolysis)
The polymer expanded and cracked the bone
